content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To draw a baseball cap, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Sketch the small button on the very top of the crown (45 seconds)
Step 2. Research different styles of vintage caps (20 minutes)
Step 3. Draw the vertical seam running down the center front (2 minutes)
Step 4. Add decorative double-stitching along the brim edge (10 minutes)
Step 5. Apply a final fixative spray to the drawing (5 minutes)
Step 6. Add a manufacturer's holographic sticker to the brim (1 minute)
Step 7. Outline the main dome of the crown (3 minutes)
Step 8. Sketch the curved line where the crown meets the brim (2 minutes)
Step 9. Gather high-quality graphite pencils and an eraser (5 minutes)
Step 10. Draw the circular ventilation eyelets on each panel (4 minutes)
Step 11. Add light cross-hatching to create fabric texture (15 minutes)
Step 12. Select the appropriate weight of drawing paper (2 minutes)
Step 13. Shade the underside of the visor to create depth (8 minutes)
Step 14. Sketch the plastic snap-back closure at the rear (5 minutes)
Step 15. Lightly map out the perspective grid (10 minutes)
Step 16. Draw a small brand tag near the back closure (3 minutes)
Step 17. Clean up stray pencil marks with a kneaded eraser (4 minutes)
Step 18. Determine the direction of the primary light source (2 minutes)
Step 19. Sharpen all pencils to a fine point (3 minutes)
Step 20. Sketch the forehead reinforcement panel (4 minutes)
Step 21. Measure the proportions of the crown height (5 minutes)
Step 22. Darken the deepest shadows in the fabric folds (6 minutes)
Step 23. Draw the side panels of the crown (7 minutes)
Step 24. Define the outer edge of the bill (3 minutes)
Step 25. Set up a desk lamp for consistent lighting (5 minutes)
Step 26. Sign the bottom corner of the artwork (1 minute)
Step 27. Design a custom logo for the front of the cap (30 minutes)
Step 28. Add sweatband detail visible from the side (4 minutes)
Step 29. Draw the squiggled lines of a crumpled fabric effect (6 minutes)
Step 30. Lay down a base layer of light grey tone (12 minutes)
Step 31. Sketch the ponytail hole above the strap (2 minutes)
Step 32. Add thickness to the edge of the visor (4 minutes)
Step 33. Clear the workspace of any dust or debris (2 minutes)
Step 34. Detail the embroidered edges of the front logo (25 minutes)
Step 35. Draw the thread loops within the embroidery (15 minutes)
Step 36. Sketch the internal buckram lining (8 minutes)
Step 37. Add mid-tone values to the side panels (12 minutes)
Step 38. Study the way light hits polyester fabric (15 minutes)
Step 39. Refine the elliptical shape of the cap opening (5 minutes)
Step 40. Draw the shadow cast by the cap on the ground (10 minutes)
Step 41. Sketch the top-stitching on the crown seams (12 minutes)
Step 42. Blend the graphite with a paper stump (10 minutes)
Step 43. Position the cap at a three-quarters angle (2 minutes)
Step 44. Add subtle wrinkles near the button (5 minutes)
Step 45. Draw the initial bounding box for the cap (3 minutes)
Step 46. Contrast the highlight on the top of the brim (7 minutes)
Step 47. Tape the paper down to the drawing board (2 minutes)
Step 48. Apply dark graphite to the recessed areas (9 minutes)
Step 49. Smooth out the transitions between light and dark (15 minutes)
Step 50. Add reflected light on the back curve (4 minutes)
Step 51. Detail the individual plastic pegs of the snap-back (6 minutes)
Step 52. Accentuate the curve of the visor (3 minutes)
Step 53. Draw the fabric grain on the brim (10 minutes)
Step 54. Erase the initial construction lines (5 minutes)
Step 55. Look at reference photos of athletic headwear (10 minutes)
Step 56. Sketch the interior labels and tags (6 minutes)
Step 57. Add a slight curve to the front panel (3 minutes)
Step 58. Refine the silhouette of the entire hat (8 minutes)
Step 59. Use a white gel pen for extreme highlights (4 minutes)
Step 60. Draw the stitching on the back adjustment strap (7 minutes)
Step 61. Sketch the general oval for the head space (2 minutes)
Step 62. Block in the basic geometric shapes (5 minutes)
Step 63. Detail the fabric overlap at the seams (5 minutes)
Step 64. Establish the horizon line (1 minute)
Step 65. Clean the drawing surface (2 minutes)
Step 66. Adjust the perspective of the brim (6 minutes)
Step 67. Sketch the basic triangular sections of the crown (4 minutes)
Step 68. Define the width of the front two panels (3 minutes)
Step 69. Add the top-down view of the visor (5 minutes)
Step 70. Draw the slight indentation on the crown top (4 minutes)
Step 71. Add frayed thread details for a "worn" look (8 minutes)
Step 72. Mark the center point of the visor (2 minutes)
Step 73. Prepare a range of pencils from 2H to 6B (4 minutes)
Step 74. Shade the interior of the cap (12 minutes)
Step 75. Compare the sketch to a real baseball cap (10 minutes)
Step 76. Darken the line weight of the foreground edges (5 minutes)
Step 77. Draw the six-panel structure lines (6 minutes)
Step 78. Select a reference cap to draw (5 minutes)
Step 79. Soften the edges of the crown (4 minutes)
Step 80. Add the price tag plastic cord (2 minutes)
Step 81. Measure the angle of the visor (3 minutes)
Step 82. Apply final deep blacks to the shadows (10 minutes)
Step 83. Organize the drawing tools (3 minutes)
Step 84. Calibrate the workspace lighting (5 minutes)
Step 85. Sketch the raised embroidery outline (8 minutes)
Step 86. Draw the mesh pattern for a trucker-style variant (15 minutes)
Step 87. Check the overall symmetry of the cap (5 minutes)
Step 88. Add a signature date (30 seconds)
Step 89. Review the tonal balance (5 minutes)
Step 90. Highlight the texture of the eyelet stitching (6 minutes)
